source_groups.label: Original Chapter LXXXIV vocational suitability and missing natal time
claims: Chap LXXXIV Profession Magistery or Trade
The chapter asks what profession or trade a child might supposedly be suited for.
Historical occupation classification without demonstrated predictive accuracy.
County people childrens Nativities not time
The initial case concerns rural families who do not know their children's exact birth times.
This is a horary workaround, not a reconstructed natal birth chart.
parents desirous what profession Sonn fittest
Parents seek advice about a particular son's occupational prospects.
No identified family or long-term observed career outcome.
Lilly prescribes casting a new figure at the time the question is asked.
Question time is different from the unknown time of birth.
He begins by inspecting the ascendant and its ruler, plus the tenth house and tenth lord.
Separate house roles without quantified prediction weights.

source_groups.label: Mars and Venus as trade significators, relative strength and Aries branch
claims: The author calls Mars and Venus special signifiers of magistery, trade and profession.
The source's glyphs are read as Mars/Venus; independent complete diplomatic reading not claimed.
He instructs choosing the stronger of the two planets before interpreting its sign.
Relative strength thresholds and contradictory dignity cases unspecified.
The stronger planet's zodiac sign guides career classification.
A single-sign taxonomy, not observed behavior.
He begins an Aries-based example rather than giving identical detail for every sign.
Aries branch requires additional angular factors.
He asks whether a planet occupies any of the chart's four angles.
Angular occupancy is an extra condition.
Planet fiery sign or nature Aries
The angular planet should be in a fire sign or share the character of Aries.
The source distinguishes sign placement from planetary likeness.

source_groups.label: Aries: cattle, wheelwright, husbandry, smith and status dignity
claims: Lilly associates the Aries case with cart making and coach making.
Historical proposed occupations, no human follow-up.
He also names shepherding, grazing and driving livestock.
Many possible matches in one branch.
deal in Cattle Groom Master Horse
The branch extends to cattle trading and tending or training horses.
Multiple cattle-related roles, not a unique forecast.
He lists farriery, butchery, brick making and smithing.
Craft catalogue, not an independently observed aptitude.
He says Mars's dignity in the key place, or the Sun's involvement, adds strength.
Ambiguous grammar of dignity and luminary involvement remains.
Under those favorable circumstances a profession using fire is predicted.
He treats the significator's exaltation as a further status-related condition.
He argues that an exalted significator may favor service to royalty or nobility rather than a servile craft.
Socioeconomic hierarchy is a period judgment, not modern career guidance.

source_groups.label: Cross-sign shape categories, people, fowl and water
claims: all Signs shape four footed Cattle
He introduces a supplementary taxonomy based on the animal/figure represented by zodiac signs.
Do not turn this into a modern vocational assessment scale.
These five signs are associated with four-footed livestock.
Gemini, Libra and Aquarius are associated with human figures.
Categorization describes zodiac iconography, not actual people.
Gemini receives an alternative association with flying birds.
One sign permits multiple occupational motifs.
Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces in the angles are taken as water-related signs.
He associates those watery/angular signs with fish or water birds and related things.
Symbolic categories, not actual animal classification.
if no Planet therein nature water
If no planet occupies those places he still makes a broad water-nature inference.
Vague fallback weakens precision; preserve as stated.

source_groups.label: Taurus: farming, husbandry, livestock and household manufacturing
claims: The vocational significator in Taurus triggers this catalogue.
Different branch from preceding Aries example.
Lilly proposes farming, planting trees and gardening.
He includes grain commerce and cattle grazing.
Trading and cultivation are separate possibilities.
He names handling oxen, cows, sheep and pigs.
Detailed livestock examples rather than proof of aptitude.
He associates Taurus with household work or trades then labeled women's matters.
Historical gender stereotype, not a valid aptitude observation.
He adds soap manufacture, cloth fulling and whitening work.
Source spelling and exact obsolete occupation identities may need specialist checking.

source_groups.label: Gemini: mathematical, clerical and surveying vocations
claims: Gemini is the specified sign for this alternative trade catalogue.
Not the same as earlier Gemini/fowl iconography.
Lilly names scribe, clerk and arithmetic practitioner.
He includes a bailiff responsible for collecting rents.
He also proposes astronomy, astrology and painting.
Multiple unrelated target jobs within one sign.

source_groups.label: Leo: heat, hunting, cattle treatment and skilled crafts
claims: The vocational planet placed in Leo triggers these examples.
Lilly names domestic service and trades involving fire or heat.
He includes hunting and treating cattle diseases.
The latter is historical veterinary medicine, not contemporary health advice.
He lists riding, horse dealing and coach work.
Equestrian roles can overlap with Aries.
He includes metalworking, watch making and glass making.

source_groups.label: Virgo: education, accounts, printing, politics and astrology
claims: Lilly suggests secretary to a king or nobleman.
Social patronage is implied by profession.
He adds politician, astrologer and a person of divinatory interests.
This is a symbolic personality/vocation assertion, not a psychological diagnosis.

source_groups.label: Libra: arts, speech, textiles, instruction and emancipation
claims: Libra is the sign used for these occupations.
He associates Libra with poetry and public speaking.
He includes silk and linen commerce.
He adds tutoring and assisting captives' release.

source_groups.label: Scorpio: medical trades, metalworking and brewing
claims: Scorpio applies to the principal trade significator.
No actual birth or profession observed.
Lilly lists surgery, pharmacy and medicine.
Not grounds for choosing a medical career or diagnosing competence.
He names brass work and metal founding.
Craft jobs not linked by demonstrated causation.
He includes brewing, wine dealing and malting.
He also suggests water-related transport work.

source_groups.label: Sagittarius: livestock commerce, chemistry, clergy and food work
claims: Lilly includes cattle buying and selling.
Overlaps Taurus/Aries rather than providing a unique signature.
He suggests pursuit of chemistry or alchemy.
Period chymistry must not be equated directly to modern chemistry.
Religious profession, not a moral or spiritual diagnosis.
He also names cooking and baking.
Food craft is a different occupational class.

source_groups.label: Capricorn: supplies, farming, metal and animal occupations
claims: He suggests candle/supply work and victualling.
He includes farriery and treatment of cattle.
Wool Lead Country commodities Husband man
He adds wool/lead commerce, country goods and husbandry.

source_groups.label: Aquarius: ships, water-related aspects and mercantile skills
claims: Aquarius introduces a maritime occupational branch.
Aquarius is categorized with human signs elsewhere; preserve both.
Lilly predicts aptitude for ship carpentry.
A distinct craft without independent job outcome.
An aspect from a planet in a water sign is an additional prerequisite for other maritime roles.
He proposes sailor or ship master under that water-aspect qualification.
Junior and senior roles are alternative outcomes.
He adds ship trimming or painting.
Merchandising can overlap other signs; not a calibrated career test.

source_groups.label: Pisces: entertainment, brewing/fish and derogatory aptitude claim
claims: Pisces introduces the final listed sign branch.
Lilly names jester, singer and gambler.
Gambling is a historical trade reference, not advice to gamble.
He includes brewer and fish seller.
He derogatorily characterizes some children in this sign as dull or foolish.
Historically pejorative claim; not evidence of intelligence, neurodevelopment, or personal worth.

This is a separate dated historical war/office case, navigation only.
